title: Constrained Subsequence Sum
statement: Choose a non-empty subsequence such that any two consecutive chosen elements are at most k indices apart. Return the largest possible sum of the chosen elements.
reference_solution:
from collections import deque
def constrainedSubsetSum(nums, k):
    dp = [0] * len(nums)
    dq = deque()
    best = float('-inf')
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        while dq and dq[0] < i - k:
            dq.popleft()
        dp[i] = x + (dp[dq[0]] if dq and dp[dq[0]] > 0 else 0)
        best = max(best, dp[i])
        while dq and dp[dq[-1]] <= dp[i]:
            dq.pop()
        dq.append(i)
    return best

hints.1_question: Let dp[i] be the best sum of a valid subsequence that ends at i. What can the previous chosen element be?
hints.2_nudge: dp[i] = nums[i] + max(0, best dp[j] for j in the last k positions). You only need the window maximum of dp, and it slides.
hints.3_big_hint: Keep a deque of indices with decreasing dp values. Drop expired indices from the front, dp[i] = nums[i] + max(0, dp[front]), then pop smaller dp values from the back and push i.

known_bugs.name: always extends the previous best even when it is negative
